chunks: Moses chose seventy of his people for His appointment, so when the tremor seized them, he said: 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before this and me. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? It is but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers.'
ai.seo_question: What was the supplication of Moses (AS) when the tremor struck the seventy men of his people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the intercessory role of the Prophet (AS) and the concept of divine decree (Qadr), where God's 'misguidance' of the foolish is often viewed as a consequence of their own choices rather than arbitrary predestination. The supplication underscores the balance between divine justice and mercy, affirming that while God guides whom He wills, He is also the ultimate source of forgiveness for those who seek it. This event serves as a model for communal repentance, emphasizing that the leader's plea can secure mercy for the broader community even amidst specific trials.
